description: The backend of a city ride-hailing service: fare estimates, ride booking, driver matching, cancellations and promo codes.

issues.title: Riders can cancel rides that are already completed
issues.symptoms: Support sees completed trips flipping to 'cancelled' after the fact, sometimes with a cancellation fee added to a trip the rider already paid for.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancelling a completed ride is rejected with a ConflictError.
A rejected cancellation leaves the completed ride unchanged (status, cancellation time and fee).
Rides in the requested or accepted status can still be cancelled.
hints: Look at cancelRide and compare its checks with the other ride actions such as startRide and completeRide.
cancelRide only refuses rides that are already cancelled. Every other status, including completed, is let through.
The module already defines which statuses may move to 'cancelled'. cancelRide should respect that rule before it changes anything.
Call assertTransition(ride, 'cancelled') at the start of cancelRide instead of only checking for the cancelled status.

context.affected: Finance is reconciling refunds against trips that were cancelled after completion.
context.priority: High: it corrupts completed-trip records and can charge riders wrongly.
context.outOfScope: Do not change the cancellation fee amount or the free window.
context.reproduce: 1. Book a ride and accept it. 2. Start it, then complete it. 3. Call cancelRide on the same ride. 4. Notice the ride is now cancelled and may carry a fee.

guide.alex: Start in rideService.js. The TRANSITIONS table and assertTransition guard accepting, starting and completing. Trace what cancelRide does before it mutates the ride and compare it with those functions.
guide.sarah: Try cancelling a ride in every status: requested, accepted, started, completed, cancelled. Check the ride object afterwards, not only whether an error was thrown.
guide.daniel: This is a missing guard clause: a state machine only protects you if every action checks that the current state allows it. Ask which states should be allowed to reach 'cancelled'.

issues.title: Riders are charged a cancellation fee at exactly the 2-minute mark
issues.symptoms: Riders who cancel right on the 2-minute mark after a driver accepts are charged a fee, even though the app promises free cancellation within 2 minutes.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancelling exactly 120 seconds after acceptance is free.
Cancelling even a moment after 120 seconds is charged the cancellation fee.
A ride cancelled at exactly 120 seconds carries a cancellation fee of 0.
hints: Open cancellationFee and look at how it decides whether the rider is still inside the free window.
The window is meant to include its last second, but the comparison treats 120 seconds as already outside it.
Think about which comparison operator includes the boundary value, and change that one comparison.
In cancellationFee, change the strict less-than against freeWindowSeconds to less-than-or-equal.

context.affected: A few hundred riders a week sit on the boundary and complain on social media.
context.priority: Medium: a trust issue with riders, not a revenue emergency.
context.outOfScope: Do not change the fee amount or the length of the free window in config.js.
context.reproduce: 1. Book a ride and accept it at time T. 2. Cancel it at T + 120 seconds. 3. Observe a fee of 5000 paise. 4. Cancelling at T + 119 seconds is free.

guide.alex: Look at cancellationFee in fareService.js and at CANCELLATION in config.js. rideService.cancelRide calls the function with the accept and cancel timestamps in milliseconds.
guide.sarah: Test 119, 120 and 121 seconds, plus 120 seconds and 1 millisecond. Also check a ride that was never accepted.
guide.daniel: This is a boundary (off-by-one) bug. When a rule says 'within N', decide whether N itself is inside, then pick the operator that matches. Write the boundary values down before coding.

issues.title: Surge pricing barely changes the fare on long trips
issues.symptoms: During a surge, riders on long trips pay almost the same as normal while the 2x banner is showing. Ops says revenue during surge is far below forecast.
acceptanceCriteria: With a surge multiplier, the whole fare (base, distance and time charges) is multiplied.
A short trip under surge is priced on base, distance and time together.
Fares without surge and the minimum fare behave as before.
hints: Read estimateFare from top to bottom and see which amounts the surge multiplier is applied to.
The multiplier is only applied to the base fare. The distance and time charges are added afterwards without it.
Add up the three charges first, then apply the multiplier to that subtotal, round once, and still enforce the minimum fare.
Compute subtotal = base + distance + time, then surged = Math.round(subtotal * surgeMultiplier), then take the larger of surged and the minimum fare.

context.affected: Every surged trip is undercharged, and longer trips are undercharged the most.
context.priority: High: it costs revenue on every busy evening.
context.outOfScope: Do not change the per-km, per-minute or minimum fare values, or the validation rules.
context.reproduce: 1. Estimate a 10 km, 20 minute trip with no surge: 20000 paise. 2. Estimate the same trip with a 1.5 multiplier. 3. Expect 30000 paise, get 22500.

guide.alex: estimateFare in fareService.js is the only function involved. requestRide in rideService.js calls it and stores the total as the ride fare.
guide.sarah: Try surge 1, 1.5 and 2 with a long and a very short trip. Work out the expected number by hand first and watch the rounding. A tiny trip with no surge should still hit the minimum fare.
guide.daniel: Order of operations matters: a multiplier should apply to the combined amount, not part of it. Be careful where rounding happens.

issues.title: The same rider can use a one-time promo code again
issues.symptoms: Some riders are getting the welcome discount on several rides. It seems to happen when they type the code in lower case.
acceptanceCriteria: A promo typed in lower case cannot be redeemed twice by the same rider.
Changing the case or spacing of an already used code does not allow another redemption.
Different riders can still redeem the promo once each.
hints: Look at what redeem stores when it succeeds and what it compares when it checks for an earlier use.
Codes are looked up case-insensitively, but the redemption is recorded with the code exactly as the rider typed it, while the check compares against the stored promo code.
Record the redemption under the same normalised code that the duplicate check uses.
In redeem, push promo.code (not the typed code) into store.redemptions.

context.affected: Marketing noticed budget burning faster than expected on the welcome promo.
context.priority: High: each extra use is real discount money.
context.outOfScope: Do not change how discounts are calculated or the expiry rules.
context.reproduce: 1. Redeem 'save20' for rider r-1. 2. Redeem 'save20' again for r-1. 3. Notice the second redemption succeeds. 4. Try 'SAVE20' as well.

guide.alex: promoService.redeem does the lookup with findPromo, then checks store.redemptions. Compare the value used for the lookup, the value written to redemptions and the value compared.
guide.sarah: Redeem with 'SAVE20', 'save20', ' Save20 ' for the same rider and a second rider, in different orders. Inspect store.redemptions after each call.
guide.daniel: This is a normalisation mismatch: the same identifier written two ways. Pick one canonical form and use it everywhere you store or compare it.

issues.title: Drivers stay unavailable after cancelled rides and get matched from old locations
issues.symptoms: Dispatch says drivers vanish from the pool after a rider cancels, and drivers who just finished a trip get requests as if they were still at the pickup spot.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancelling an accepted ride makes its driver available again.
After a completed ride the driver's location is the drop-off point, so matching uses their real position.
A driver on an active ride is not matched to another ride until that ride ends.
hints: Follow a driver through acceptRide, completeRide and cancelRide and check the driver's status and location after each.
Two things go wrong: cancelRide never gives the driver back, and releaseDriver accepts a location that it then ignores.
cancelRide must release the driver of an accepted ride, and releaseDriver must record the new location when one is passed in.
Call driverService.releaseDriver(ride.driverId) in cancelRide when the ride has a driver, and in releaseDriver set driver.location to the given location when there is one.

context.affected: Dispatch capacity looks lower than it is and pickup ETAs are wrong, so riders wait longer.
context.priority: High: it hurts matching quality in every busy period.
context.outOfScope: Do not change the matching distance calculation or the ride status rules.
context.reproduce: 1. Accept a ride so the only driver becomes busy. 2. Cancel the ride. 3. Book another ride: no driver is available. 4. Complete a trip and check the driver's location.

guide.alex: Read driverService.js first: findNearestAvailable uses status and location. Then follow where rideService.js calls markBusy and releaseDriver, and where it does not.
guide.sarah: Use a store with one driver, then with two. Cancel an accepted ride, complete a ride far from the pickup and then request a ride near the drop-off. Check getDriver after each step.
guide.daniel: State that is set in one place must be undone in every exit path, and a parameter that is accepted but never used is a warning sign. Check every way a ride can end.
